finalText:
---

## Root Cause Diagnosis

**Root-cause resource:** `pod/c038-pending` (the pod itself is the problem — there is no upstream controller or other resource involved.)

**Root-cause mechanism:** The pod spec contains a **hardcoded `nodeSelector`** that pins scheduling to a nonexistent node:

```json
{
  "kubernetes.io/hostname": "node-does-not-exist"
}
```

No node in the cluster has the hostname `node-does-not-exist`. The scheduler rejects every one of the 368 nodes — the 5 candidates that survive taint/unschedulable filters are all eliminated because they don't match the node selector.

### Evidence

| Source | Finding |
|---|---|
| `kubectl describe pod` | `Node-Selectors: kubernetes.io/hostname=node-does-not-exist` |
| Pod condition | `PodScheduled: False` |
| Scheduling event | `0/368 nodes are available: ... 5 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector` |
| Pod status | `Pending`, `0/1`, node `<none>`, no IP assigned |
| Pod spec JSON | Confirmed `nodeSelector.kubernetes.io/hostname = "node-does-not-exist"` |

### Impact scope

Single pod: `c038-pending`. No downstream cascading — this is a standalone pod with no ReplicaSet/Deployment owner. The container (`busybox:1.36` running `sleep 3600`) is lightweight (20m CPU / 32Mi memory requested) and would schedule fine on any available node without the nodeSelector.

### Confidence

**High** — the nodeSelector value is a fabricated hostname that clearly does not match any node in the cluster. The scheduler event explicitly attributes 5 of the 368 rejections to the node selector mismatch, and no other scheduling constraints (taints, tolerations, affinity, resource limits) are present.

### Remediation

Remove the `nodeSelector` from the pod spec so it can be scheduled on any available node:

```bash
kubectl patch pod c038-pending -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602 \
  --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/nodeSelector"}]'
```

Or, if the pod was intentionally targeting a specific node, update the selector to match an actual hostname:

```bash
kubectl patch pod c038-pending -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602 \
  --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/nodeSelector","value":{"kubernetes.io/hostname":"<actual-node-name>"}}]'
```

Since this is a standalone pod (no controller), after the patch the scheduler will pick it up immediately and bind it to an eligible node.

## Root Cause Diagnosis

**Root-cause resource:** `pod/c038-pending` (the pod itself is the problem — there is no upstream controller or other resource involved.)

**Root-cause mechanism:** The pod spec contains a **hardcoded `nodeSelector`** that pins scheduling to a nonexistent node:

```json
{
  "kubernetes.io/hostname": "node-does-not-exist"
}
```

No node in the cluster has the hostname `node-does-not-exist`. The scheduler rejects every one of the 368 nodes — the 5 candidates that survive taint/unschedulable filters are all eliminated because they don't match the node selector.

### Evidence

| Source | Finding |
|---|---|

| Pod condition | `PodScheduled: False` |
| Scheduling event | `0/368 nodes are available: ... 5 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector` |
| Pod status | `Pending`, `0/1`, node `<none>`, no IP assigned |
| Pod spec JSON | Confirmed `nodeSelector.kubernetes.io/hostname = "node-does-not-exist"` |

### Impact scope

Single pod: `c038-pending`. No downstream cascading — this is a standalone pod with no ReplicaSet/Deployment owner. The container (`busybox:1.36` running `sleep 3600`) is lightweight (20m CPU / 32Mi memory requested) and would schedule fine on any available node without the nodeSelector.

### Confidence

**High** — the nodeSelector value is a fabricated hostname that clearly does not match any node in the cluster. The scheduler event explicitly attributes 5 of the 368 rejections to the node selector mismatch, and no other scheduling constraints (taints, tolerations, affinity, resource limits) are present.

### Remediation

Remove the `nodeSelector` from the pod spec so it can be scheduled on any available node:

```bash
kubectl patch pod c038-pending -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602 \
  --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/nodeSelector"}]'
```

Or, if the pod was intentionally targeting a specific node, update the selector to match an actual hostname:

```bash
kubectl patch pod c038-pending -n siclaw-eval-yye-20260602 \
  --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/nodeSelector","value":{"kubernetes.io/hostname":"<actual-node-name>"}}]'
```

Since this is a standalone pod (no controller), after the patch the scheduler will pick it up immediately and bind it to an eligible node.
